source_title: Tutor Perini Corporation Form 10-K (fiscal 2023) and fourth-quarter/full-year 2023 results
publisher_issuer: Tutor Perini Corporation (SEC Form 10-K and results release)
company_context: Tutor Perini is a large U.S. civil, building, and specialty construction contractor. For years it carried elevated unbilled receivables and disputed change-order/claim balances (notably in its Specialty Contractors segment in New York) that tied up working capital pending litigation or negotiated resolution. Beginning in 2022 it prioritized faster resolution of disputed matters to convert balances to cash, and in 2023 it reported record operating cash flow even while still posting a net loss.
business_type: Large civil, building, and specialty construction / engineering contractor (long-cycle, percentage-of-completion revenue with claims and change orders)
macro_context: Post-pandemic construction cost inflation and elevated interest rates raising the carrying cost of working capital, alongside a multi-year effort to litigate or settle long-outstanding project disputes.
outcome_category: 3 - improving / partial recovery from working-capital stress (still loss-making but cash generation recovering)
evidence_summary: Tutor Perini's working-capital stress centered on large unbilled receivables and disputed change-order/claim balances that the company estimates as variable consideration and that often require litigation or other dispute resolution to collect. Management states it made continued progress resolving outstanding disputes and reducing unbilled receivables, expecting to resolve the majority of remaining disputed matters by the end of 2024, and that in 2022 it prioritized faster resolution of disputed matters (primarily Specialty Contractors in New York) to convert balances to cash more quickly. The cash-conversion effort showed results: net cash provided by operating activities was $308.5 million in 2023, the largest since the 2008 Tutor-Saliba/Perini merger and up from the prior record of $207.0 million in 2022, even as the company reported a 2023 net loss of $171.2 million (improved from a $210.0 million net loss in 2022) and backlog grew 28 percent to $10.2 billion. This is a documented working-capital-stress case on a recovering trajectory rather than a clean failure or a clean success.

source_backed_metrics.working_capital_driver: elevated unbilled receivables and disputed change-order/claim balances requiring litigation or negotiated resolution

owner_decision_context: Management deliberately prioritized resolving long-outstanding disputed claims and unbilled receivables to convert tied-up balances into cash, accepting continued reported losses while improving cash generation.
action_taken: Accelerated resolution of disputed matters and change-order claims (notably Specialty Contractors in New York), targeting resolution of the majority of remaining disputes by end of 2024 and converting unbilled receivables to cash.
outcome_evidence: Operating cash flow rose to a record $308.5 million in 2023 from $207.0 million in 2022; net loss narrowed to $171.2 million from $210.0 million; backlog grew 28 percent to $10.2 billion, indicating partial recovery from working-capital stress while still loss-making.
source_limitations: SEC EDGAR filing page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; the qualitative receivables/dispute narrative was confirmed in search snippets attributed to the 2023 10-K, and the cash-flow, net-loss, and backlog figures were confirmed in named-source results-release snippets (MarketScreener, le lezard, Eagle Tribune) rather than read in full filing text. Specific unbilled-receivables dollar balances were not captured verbatim and are therefore omitted from source_backed_metrics. The trajectory is recovering, so this is a borderline outcome-3 case rather than active distress.
directly_stated: Working capital tied up in unbilled receivables and disputed change-order/claim balances requiring dispute resolution
Management made continued progress reducing unbilled receivables, expecting most disputes resolved by end of 2024
In 2022 prioritized faster resolution of disputed matters (Specialty Contractors, New York) to convert to cash
2023 operating cash flow $308.5 million, a record, up from $207.0 million in 2022
2023 net loss $171.2 million ($3.30/share); 2022 net loss $210.0 million
inferred: Long-cycle contract accounting with disputed claims is the structural source of the working-capital stress
Cash conversion is recovering even though the income statement still shows losses, making the diagnosis trajectory-dependent
why_useful_for_opsiq: A documented working_capital_stress case in construction/engineering where receivables and disputed claims, not income-statement demand, drive the cash strain, and where cash generation is recovering while losses persist. Useful for testing whether OpsIQ distinguishes working-capital/receivables stress from a solvency or demand failure, and whether it correctly reads an improving-but-still-loss-making trajectory rather than over-calling distress.
